text: Luke opens his second letter to Theophilus, recalling that his first book covered everything Jesus did and taught from the very start.
That account ran up to the day Jesus was taken up to heaven, after he had used the Holy Spirit to give final orders to the apostles he had picked out.
Following his suffering, Jesus showed himself alive to them again and again over forty days, offering plenty of convincing evidence and talking with them about God's kingdom.
On one occasion while eating together, he told them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait there for what the Father had promised, something he had already described to them.
John, he said, baptized with water, but before many more days pass you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit instead.
When they were gathered, they asked him whether this was the moment he would give Israel its kingdom back.
He answered that knowing the exact timing was not their business — the Father alone controls those dates.
Instead, he said, you will be given power once the Holy Spirit arrives, and you will tell people about me everywhere — Jerusalem, all of Judea, Samaria, and to the farthest corners of the earth.
As soon as he said this, he was lifted off the ground while they watched, and a cloud swallowed him from view.
They kept staring upward as he disappeared, until suddenly two men dressed in white were standing right beside them.
The men asked why the Galileans were still staring at the sky, and promised that this same Jesus, taken from them into heaven, would return exactly the way they had just watched him leave.
They walked back to Jerusalem from the hill known as the Mount of Olives, a short distance the law allowed for travel on the Sabbath.

Once inside the city they went up to the room where they had been lodging — Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
All of them kept praying together with one purpose, joined by a number of women, Jesus' mother Mary, and his own brothers.
Some days later Peter got up in front of the believers, a crowd of roughly a hundred twenty, and spoke.
Friends, he said, the Scripture had to come true — the words the Holy Spirit gave through David long ago about Judas, who led the men that arrested Jesus.
Judas, after all, had been counted as one of us and had shared fully in this ministry.
With the money he earned from his treachery he obtained a plot of land, and there he fell headfirst and his body split open, spilling everything inside.
Word of it spread through everyone in Jerusalem, and in their own language they began calling that plot Akeldama, meaning Field of Blood.
For it stands written in the book of Psalms, 'let his home become empty, with no one left to live there,' and also, 'let someone else take over his position.'
So, Peter continued, we need someone from among the men who traveled with us the entire time the Lord Jesus was among us,
starting from John's baptism until the day Jesus was taken up — this person must join us as a witness to his resurrection.
They put forward two men: Joseph, known as Barsabbas and also called Justus, and Matthias.
Then they prayed, asking the Lord, who knows what is in every heart, to show them which of the two he had chosen
to take up the apostolic work Judas abandoned when he went where he belonged.
They drew lots between them, the lot landed on Matthias, and he was added to the eleven apostles.
